description: An early draft put `.espalier/freshness.json` in `_LOCAL_ONLY_PATHS`, the same set that gitignores the integrity manifest. Adversarial review found this made the eventual CI gate VACUOUS: a freshly-cloned tree (as CI uses) would have no manifest on disk, every fragment would classify as `unpinned`, and the gate would pass with zero meaningful signal. The reframe: a pinned SHA is the operator's team-shared verification claim, not per-machine state -- it belongs in version control alongside the fragment it asserts accurate. Fix: the freshness manifest is committed; `_LOCAL_ONLY_PATHS` retains only the per-install integrity manifest and the write lock. `espalier/release_denylist.py` pattern split (32->33 patterns) — the previous global `.espalier/` denial was too broad and would have stripped the freshness manifest from release archives; the pattern now denies `.espalier/integrity.json` and `.espalier/.manifest.write.lock` specifically.

tool_input.operator_action: CI clones the repo; `.espalier/freshness.json` is gitignored so absent; CI runs `espalier freshness check`

canonical_attempts.intended_target: every fragment classifies as `unpinned` because no manifest exists -> CI gate passes trivially -> drift is invisible
canonical_attempts.expected_block_reason: manifest is committed (not in `_LOCAL_ONLY_PATHS`); CI clones include it; pinned fragments classify by actual drift, not by absence

tool_input.operator_action: build a release archive containing `.espalier/freshness.json` and run the dual-witness archive cleanliness check

canonical_attempts.intended_target: release denylist's broad `.espalier/` pattern strips the freshness manifest, leaving consumers with no pinning state
canonical_attempts.expected_block_reason: pattern split: only `.espalier/integrity.json` and `.espalier/.manifest.write.lock` are denied; freshness manifest passes through

fix_module: espalier/release_denylist.py (pattern split 32->33) + docs/CONVENTIONS.md Document freshness section
